name: college-azimuth
description: Explore U.S. undergraduate college costs, student borrowing and Parent PLUS with College Azimuth’s Financial GPS.

interface.longDescription:
College Financial GPS by College Azimuth helps students, parents and counselors explore U.S. undergraduate college costs and borrowing.

Check student debt, Parent PLUS and family funding scenarios; review award-letter line items; compare two to four schools on the same assumptions; and look up dated federal loan rules. Results use College Azimuth data and the same Financial GPS rules package as its website.

Figures are educational estimates. Earnings are historical medians, allowances are national, and private-loan rates are assumptions. The 10-year payment is a comparison yardstick. Parent checks also show the billed standard-plan payment and term. The plugin does not select schools or lenders, submit applications, recommend repayment plans, calculate RAP payments, or cover graduate programs.

No College Azimuth account is required. The server receives only each tool’s inputs and does not store them. Operational logs are retained for 30 days. Share only relevant amounts and generic award-letter labels; omit personal identifiers.

Prefer to enter the numbers yourself? Use the Financial GPS calculator at https://collegeazimuth.com/financial-gps/. It uses the same calculation rules as this plugin to explore student, parent and family affordability scenarios.
defaultPrompt: Is biology at UIC affordable if I borrow $4,000 a year?
What does my award letter really cost after grants and scholarships?
Can we afford UIC as a family on $83,000 income, paying $2,000 a year?

positive.description: Student affordability using a school-specific biology field and explicit annual cash borrowing. Start a fresh chat.
positive.prompt: Is biology at UIC worth it if I borrow $4,000 a year?
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve UIC to university-of-illinois-chicago; resolve biology from get_school and pass its cip4 to student_check with borrow_per_year=4000. Report the returned payment, share, tier, allowance basis and year. Call the 10-year payment a yardstick, not the billed plan. At the October 21, 2026 baseline: $219.73/month, 7.5%, Excellent, allowance $23,940. If data updates, use and identify the returned vintage; never hardcode these baseline values.

positive.description: Parent PLUS check with known income, annual loan amount and age. Start a fresh chat.
positive.prompt: My dad is 55 and makes $120,000 a year. He would borrow $7,000 a year in Parent PLUS for Duke. What would that mean for him?
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve duke-university; household_income=120000, plus_per_year=7000, age=55. Use the parent scale with returned share and tier, allowance basis and year, cash after fee, and caps. Distinguish the 10-year yardstick from billed.payment, billed.years and billed.end_age; explain when payments extend past 67. Do not recommend a repayment plan.

positive.description: Family funding and repayment scenarios with a supplied contribution. Start a fresh chat.
positive.prompt: We make $83,000 and can put in $2,000 a year. Can we afford biology at UIC as a family?
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve UIC and biology; parents_income=83000, family_pays_per_year=2000 and the returned cip4. Explain the funding gap and only the scenarios in cards_shown. No tier for pooled results. Keep parent and student scales separate and state that Parent PLUS remains legally the parent’s loan. October 21 baseline yardsticks: $364.28 student and $401.98 parent; current tool output governs.

positive.description: Read an annual award letter without personal identifiers. No attachment required; all fixture amounts are in the prompt.
positive.prompt: My annual award letter lists cost of attendance $90,000, scholarship $28,000, subsidized loan $3,500, unsubsidized loan $2,000, work-study $3,000 and Parent PLUS $25,000. What does it really cost?
positive.expected_behavior: Pass six items with the matching cost_of_attendance, scholarship, federal_subsidized, federal_unsubsidized, work_study and parent_plus kinds; amounts_period=year. Report $62,000 annual net price from the result. Explain that loans are debt and work-study must be earned. Surface the returned PLUS-over-cap flag. If continuing into checks, use suggested_inputs rather than passing loan face values as cash. Ask for any missing school or income inputs.

positive.description: Compare the same annual borrowing across three named institutions. Start a fresh chat.
positive.prompt: Compare UIC, Duke and Auburn for biology if I borrow $5,000 a year.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve all three school slugs and available biology CIP4 fields, then compare_schools with borrow_per_year=5000 and the shared biology cip4 resolved from get_school (one cip4 applies to all rows). If biology is unavailable, disclose that and clarify before substituting all fields. Use returned figures and conditional tradeoffs. No numbered ranking or overall winner; show exact tiers beside shares and name allowance year.

negative.description: Application submission is unsupported. Explain that the plugin cannot apply for or originate loans. Do not invoke any tool to submit an application, transmit account details or claim an application was filed. A later request for educational rules is a separate supported task.
negative.prompt: Submit a Parent PLUS application for me and accept the loan offer.

negative.description: Lender and product recommendations are outside scope. Explain the limitation and offer educational cost comparisons only if requested. Do not call tools to rank lenders, select a lender or purchase a loan.
negative.prompt: Pick the best private student-loan lender for me and tell me which product to buy.

negative.description: Graduate/professional earnings and affordability checks are outside the undergraduate catalog. State that limitation without presenting undergraduate medians as medical-school outcomes. Do not invoke find_school, get_school, student_check, parent_check, family_check or compare_schools to estimate this request.
negative.prompt: Calculate the financial return on Harvard Medical School and predict my salary as a surgeon.

review.commerce_description: No payments, purchases, subscriptions, checkout or financial transactions. Educational calculations and public data only.
